newsitem.title: USA: Grieving U.S. mother assails diplomatic immunity.
newsitem.headline: Grieving U.S. mother assails diplomatic immunity.

text.p: The mother of a 16-year-old girl killed in a car crash allegedly caused by a Georgian diplomat who had been drinking lashed out on Monday against any deal that might let him escape prosecution.

Viviane Wagner, clutching a pink and white stuffed rabbit that belonged to her daughter Joviane Waltrick, said she did not hate Gueorgui Makharadze, 35, the diplomat accused of causing the Jan. 4 crash.

"I just want that he respond for his actions, as I would, without diplomatic immunity," she told a news conference held at the site of the accident. She vowed to keep a daily vigil there until she was satisfied that justice had been done, and urged the public to bring flowers.

Wagner, a Brazilian, said she was uncertain about the implications of a decision by Eduard Shevardnadze, the president of Georgia, to waive diplomatic immunity for Makharadze while U.S. prosecutors prepare any future case against him.

Police have said speed and alcohol both may have played a role in the five-car crash, allegedly triggered when Makharadze, travelling at 80 mph (130 kph) or faster, slammed into a car stopped for a red light at Dupont Circle in the heart of Washington. Joviane was pronounced dead shortly after the accident.

"I am not calling for the maximum sentence for Mr. Makharadze," Wagner said through an interpreter. "Surely his sentence will be less than what I have to live with, to live out the rest of my days without."
